name: m5-scaling-heap
description: Scalability with the heap scaled to the number of compiles: 1.5 GB per concurrent compile (1.5 GB at N=1 to 24 GB at N=16), G1 with regions fixed at 4 MB so the humongous threshold (2 MB) does not move with the heap size, Graal 25.4.4, on the M5 Pro (6 P + 12 E cores, 48 GB). `m5-scaling` kept the heap at 8 GB, so N compiles shared one young generation and GC pressure grew with N for both tables; here each compile has the same heap share at every N, so what changes with N is contention for cores. Hypothesis: the chained table's extra GC work (card scanning, copying, refinement) is absorbed by spare cores at small N and shows as N approaches the core count. Score is time per compile; throughput is N / score.
